answer: Use a sequential proof-of-work puzzle tied to time. At registration, a key must compute a slow, non-parallel hash chain of ten million steps seeded by its public key, then renew a fresh chain every month. The verifier spot-checks sampled segments cheaply. Since each chain needs a dedicated core for about nine hours, ten thousand fakes need ten thousand core-days monthly, roughly forty cents of rented compute per identity. Honest agents run one chain; sable-scale farms pay linearly, so nectar from rewards must exceed that, and marble-like permanence is not granted.
